title: Fewest People Behind the Survey Answers
statement:
Everyone at a festival wears a shirt of some colour. You asked some of them one question: "How many other people here wear the same colour as you?" Their honest answers are in answers. People you did not ask may exist too.

Return the smallest number of people that could be at the festival, consistent with all the answers.

examples.why: A colour where people answer 2 has exactly 3 wearers. Four people cannot fit in one such group, so there are two groups of 3.
The 0 is alone (1). The two 1s can be the same pair (2). The 3 has three unseen partners (4).
Only two people can share a colour whose answer is 1, so the third starts a new pair with someone you did not ask.

hints: If someone answers x, how many people wear their colour in total?
People who give the same answer x can share a colour, but only x + 1 of them at a time. What happens to the (x + 2)-th one?
Count how many people gave each answer. For answer x said c times you need ceil(c / (x + 1)) groups, each of size x + 1.

explain.intuition:
An answer of x means that colour has exactly x + 1 wearers. To keep the total small, put as many people with the same answer into the same colour as you can. But a group only has x + 1 slots. Once it is full, the next person who says x must belong to a new group of x + 1, and that new group counts in full even if you asked only one of its members.

People with different answers can never share a colour, because they would disagree about its size. So each answer value is solved on its own and the results are added.
steps: Count how many times each answer appears.
For answer x with count c, the group size is g = x + 1.
The number of groups is ceil(c / g); add groups · g to the total.
pitfalls: Adding x + 1 once per distinct answer. Four people answering 2 need two groups, not one.
Adding x + 1 for every person. Two people who answer 1 can be the same pair.
Mixing people with different answers into one colour. Their answers would contradict each other.

solutions.title: Count answers, round up to full groups
solutions.idea: Group equal answers. Each answer x needs ceil(count / (x + 1)) full groups of x + 1 people.

solutions.title: Open slots in one pass
solutions.idea: Track how many unclaimed slots the current group for each answer still has. When a group is full, open a new one and pay for all its members.

followups: What is the largest number of people consistent with the answers if the festival holds at most N people?
Some answers may be lies. With at most one liar, what is the smallest possible total?
